scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The loyalty dance appeared soon after the Cultural Revolution started in 1966.
In the late 1960s, Chairman Mao's cult of personality reached new heights, leading to citizens performing the dance to express political loyalty.
By 1968, 'Three Loyalties' activities reached a climax in various areas, making the dance widespread all over the country.
on_screen: Map: People's Republic of China · East Asia
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance was an everyday fixture of life in the late 1960s, practiced to display lifelong devotion to Mao Zedong and exercise total discipline.
It was closely linked to the ideological slogan of the 'Three Loyalties' (三忠于): loyalty to Chairman Mao, loyalty to Mao Zedong Thought, and loyalty to Chairman Mao's revolutionary line.
Song lyrics performed during the dance asserted that relationship with Mao was closer than that with one's own parents.
Today it is a historical tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance consisted of a simple collective dance performed in public places like plazas, squares, or at parades.
Choreographically, it did not involve much more than stretching one's arms from the heart to Mao's portrait, with basic movements originating from a folk dance popular in Xinjiang.
Hand and arm movements were consistently directed toward the sky, symbolizing respect for Mao Zedong.
Watch for Heart to portrait extension, Skyward reach.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Collective mass performance in open plazas, public squares, and parades.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance was frequently accompanied by revolutionary songs.

Key songs included 'The East is Red' (东方红), 'Beloved Chairman Mao' (敬愛的毛主席), 'Golden Hill of Beijing' (北京的金山上), and 'Sailing the Seas Depends on the Helmsman' (大海航行靠舵手), alongside musical settings featuring quotations from Chairman Mao.
Mass singing of revolutionary anthems featuring brass, choral voices, and explicit ideological lyrics.
